first.rationale: Onboarding completion and activation are both declining, and prior evidence indicates that shorter onboarding and fewer required signup fields improved completion, time-to-value, and durable first-week activation for self-serve/SMB accounts. This directly supports sustainable qualified revenue more reliably than broad promotional pricing, which carries documented retention risk. Verification will confirm experiment scope, durability, and guardrails before commitment.

mid.rationale: Run a standard, guarded onboarding-simplification experiment focused on shortening the in-product onboarding path rather than discounting. The verified shortened-flow result directly addresses both current declines: completion rose 13%, time-to-value fell 2.1 days, and 30-day retention rose 3%. For SMB entry steps, test reduced required fields separately or as a tightly bounded variant: its verified activation and qualified-revenue gains came with a 1% 30-day retention decline and have not replicated outside SMB. Measure qualified revenue and 30-day retention alongside completion and activation; do not expand beyond self-serve/SMB until results confirm durable value.

final2.rationale: Shift the single experiment to a narrowly targeted promotional-pricing test for price-sensitive SMB accounts facing competitor pressure. This is the one direction with inherited evidence for this specific competitive segment and can address acute price-driven churn conversations. Keep it tightly bounded by segment, offer duration, and incremental eligibility, because prior evidence showed materially worse 30-day retention despite acquisition and revenue lift. Evaluate retained qualified revenue, churn, and post-promotion retention—not conversion or near-term revenue alone—and do not broaden without evidence that downstream value is preserved.
